about: Names for land shapes that the historical-basemaps source leaves unnamed (they would show blank). Each fix names the unnamed shape that contains `point` [lng, lat] on the given maps. A fix with `subjectOf` also sets the shape's overlord (SUBJECTO) where the source names the wrong one; a subjectOf equal to the shape’s own name removes the overlord. A fix with `was` renames a shape that already has a misleading name. A fix with `cutAlong` {year, name, from, to} splits the shape along that map's border of `name` (from vertex `from` to vertex `to`); the part containing `point` keeps the shape and the rest becomes a new shape named `rest` (islands inside `restBox` go with it). A fix with `overlay` {from, names} copies the shapes with those names from the `from` map on top of the given maps and drops the shapes listed in `remove`. See docs/DATA.md. Applied by scripts/apply-border-fixes.mjs after downloading.

fixes.name: Switzerland
fixes.why: Source shape for Switzerland is a tiny sliver; the country itself is unnamed.

fixes.name: Taiwan
fixes.why: Unnamed in 1994; named Taiwan on the 1960 and 2000 maps.

fixes.name: Taiwan (Japan)
fixes.why: Japanese colony 1895–1945.

fixes.why: Zulu Kingdom until the Anglo-Zulu War (1879).

fixes.name: Zululand
fixes.why: Zulu Kingdom until 1879.

fixes.name: Natal

fixes.name: Natal
fixes.why: British colony of Natal.

fixes.name: Angola
fixes.why: Portuguese Angola; named on the 1914 map.

fixes.name: Tasmania (UK)
fixes.why: British colony until federation (1901).

fixes.name: Greece
fixes.why: Euboea, Greek since 1830.

fixes.name: Greece
fixes.why: Crete joined Greece in 1913.

fixes.name: Greece
fixes.why: East Thrace was under Greek control 1920–22.

fixes.name: Ottoman Sultanate
fixes.why: North-western Anatolia, Ottoman territory (Greek army advancing in 1920).

fixes.name: Russian Empire
fixes.why: Kolguyev Island, Russian.

fixes.name: Saudi Arabia
fixes.why: Najd interior, Saudi-ruled since 1921.

fixes.name: Hail
fixes.why: Rashidi Emirate of Ha’il until its conquest in 1921.

fixes.name: Seljuk Caliphate
fixes.why: The Seljuk Sultanate of Rum was an Ilkhanid vassal 1256–1308 (Wikipedia, Sultanate of Rum, checked 7 Nov 2026); the source map names the Mongol Empire, so the shape showed as the whole empire.

fixes.name: Zaire
fixes.why: Still the Belgian Congo in 1945: a Belgian colony 1908–1960 (Wikipedia, Belgian Congo, checked 7 Nov 2026); the source map gives it no overlord.

fixes.name: Greenland
fixes.why: A Danish colony until 1953 (Wikipedia, History of Greenland, checked 7 Nov 2026); the 1878 and 1880 maps name Denmark, the 1900 map gives no overlord.

fixes.name: Novgorod
fixes.why: Novgorod escaped conquest but accepted Mongol supremacy as a tributary of the Golden Horde (Wikipedia, Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus’, checked 7 Nov 2026); the source map names the whole Mongol Empire.

fixes.name: Ryazan
fixes.why: Ryazan was taken in 1237 and its princes answered to the Golden Horde, which killed two of them (Wikipedia, Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus’; Grand Principality of Ryazan, checked 7 Nov 2026); the source map names the whole Mongol Empire.

fixes.name: Naples
fixes.why: Naples stayed Spanish until 1707; it went to the Austrian Habsburgs by the Treaty of Rastatt in 1714 (Wikipedia, Kingdom of Naples, checked 7 Nov 2026). The source map names the Austrian Empire; the shape already links to the Spanish Empire.

fixes.name: Sardinia
fixes.why: Like Naples, Sardinia was still Spanish in 1700 and only passed to Austria after the War of the Spanish Succession (Wikipedia, Kingdom of Naples, checked 7 Nov 2026). The source map names the Austrian Empire; the shape already links to the Spanish Empire.

fixes.name: Parma
fixes.why: A sovereign duchy restored in 1814 and ruled by Marie Louise, Napoleon’s Habsburg wife, not part of the Austrian Empire (Wikipedia, Duchy of Parma and Piacenza, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Modena
fixes.why: A sovereign duchy ruled from 1814 by the Austria-Este branch of the House of Este, not part of the Austrian Empire (Wikipedia, Duchy of Modena and Reggio, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Congo
fixes.why: The French Congo began only on 10 September 1880 with the Brazza–Iloo treaty (Wikipedia, French Congo, checked 7 Nov 2026), so the 1878 map’s French overlord is too early.

fixes.name: South Africa
fixes.why: A self-governing dominion (Wikipedia, Union of South Africa, checked 7 Nov 2026). The source maps give Canada, Australia and New Zealand in 1914, and South Africa from 1920, no overlord, so 1914 is made the same.

fixes.name: Egypt
fixes.why: Britain recognised Egyptian independence in 1922; the Kingdom of Egypt kept British troops (in the Suez Canal zone after 1936) but was not a protectorate (Wikipedia, Kingdom of Egypt, checked 7 Nov 2026). The 1914 and 1920 maps keep Britain: protectorate 1914–1922 (Wikipedia, Sultanate of Egypt).

fixes.name: Muscat and Oman
fixes.why: Under de facto British protection only, never a formal protectorate (Wikipedia, Muscat and Oman, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Muscat and Oman
fixes.why: Under de facto British protection only, never a formal protectorate (Wikipedia, Muscat and Oman, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Oman (British Raj)
fixes.why: Same land as Muscat and Oman: de facto British protection only (Wikipedia, Muscat and Oman, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Annam
fixes.why: Bảo Đại ended the French protectorate on 11 March 1945 under Japanese sponsorship (Empire of Vietnam, March–August 1945); France did not regain Annam that year (Wikipedia, Empire of Vietnam, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Great Khanate
fixes.why: The 1400 source map repeats the 1279–1300 Yuan outline, so Korea (Goryeo was a Yuan vassal) is still drawn inside the Great Khanate. Joseon ruled Korea from 1392 (Wikipedia, Joseon, checked 9 Nov 2026). Cut along the Ming–Korea line of the 1492 map; the islands go with Korea.

fixes.name: Great Khanate
fixes.why: The same Yuan outline also covers China proper, which the Ming ruled from 1368 after the Yuan court fled north (Wikipedia, Ming dynasty and Northern Yuan, checked 9 Nov 2026). Cut along the northern border of the 1492 Ming map (approximate for 1400); the Mongolian part stays the Great Khanate (Northern Yuan).

fixes.name: Dzungar Khanate
fixes.why: This shape is Dzungaria, the Tarim Basin and western Mongolia: the Dzungar Khanate (1634–1755), which conquered the Tarim Basin in 1680 (Wikipedia, Dzungar Khanate, checked 9 Nov 2026). The source's generic label linked it to Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand. A small separate piece near Merv keeps the old label.

fixes.name: Kazakh Khanate
fixes.why: On the 1815 map this label covers the eastern and central Kazakh steppe (Astana, Balkhash, Almaty, Semey), while 'Turan' covers Khiva, Bukhara and Kokand. The Kazakh khans still ruled there: Russia abolished the Middle Jüz khanate only after 1818 and the institution in 1822–24 (Wikipedia, Kazakh Khanate, checked 9 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Cape Colony
fixes.why: The western Cape is mislabelled 'Dutch East Indies' under the Netherlands. Britain re-occupied the Cape in 1806 and the Dutch formally ceded it in 1814 (Wikipedia, Cape Colony, checked 9 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Dutch East Indies (British rule)
fixes.subjectOf: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
fixes.why: Java and the other Dutch possessions were under British rule from 1811 to 1816 and handed back on 19 August 1816 under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 (Wikipedia, French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies, checked 9 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Dutch East Indies (British rule)
fixes.subjectOf: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
fixes.why: Bangka was seized by the British expedition to Palembang in 1812 and held until 1816 (Wikipedia, French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies, checked 9 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Dutch East Indies (British rule)
fixes.subjectOf: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
fixes.why: Ternate and the Moluccas fell to Britain in 1810 and were returned with Java under the 1814 treaty (Wikipedia, French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies, checked 9 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Hong Kong
fixes.why: British rule ended with the handover on 1 July 1997 (Wikipedia, British Hong Kong, checked 7 Nov 2026).

fixes.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
fixes.why: The source map still labels this shape Fatimid Caliphate in 1200, but Saladin ended the Fatimids in 1171 and Egypt and Syria were Ayyubid (Wikipedia, Ayyubid dynasty, checked 14 Nov 2026). The shape is the source's and also covers North African land that was not Ayyubid, so it is approximate.

fixes.name: Philippines
fixes.why: Unnamed on the 1530 map, though the 1500 and 1650 maps name it; links to the pre-colonial Philippine states (before Spanish rule from 1565).

fixes.name: Philippines
fixes.why: Unnamed on the 1600 map although the Manila galleon ran from 1565. Spain ruled Luzon and the Visayas from Manila, founded in 1571 (Wikipedia, Captaincy General of the Philippines).

fixes.name: Ojibwe
fixes.why: Misspelling in the source. Ojibwe (also Ojibwa or Chippewa), as spelled elsewhere in this app.

The source’s 1600 map repeats the 1530 map for South America, so it still showed the Inca Empire (conquered 1532–72) and no colonies. By 1600 Spain ruled the Andes from Lima as the Viceroyalty of Peru (from 1542) and Portugal held the Brazilian coast (Wikipedia, Viceroyalty of Peru; Colonial Brazil). The 1650 shapes are used, so their inland edges are approximate.
